citeAs: Xinhao Li, Yi Wang, Jiashuo Yu, Xiangyu Zeng, Yuhan Zhu, Haian Huang, Jianfei Gao, Kunchang Li, Yinan He, Chenting Wang, Yu Qiao, Yali Wang, Limin Wang (2025). VideoChat-Flash: Hierarchical Compression for Long-Context Video Modeling. arXiv:2501.00574.
creator: Xinhao Li, Yi Wang, Jiashuo Yu, Xiangyu Zeng, Yuhan Zhu, Haian Huang, Jianfei Gao, Kunchang Li, Yinan He, Chenting Wang, Yu Qiao, Yali Wang, Limin Wang (Shanghai AI Laboratory, Nanjing University, Shenzhen Institutes of Advanced Technology CAS, Shanghai Innovation Institute)
description: A large-scale training dataset for long video understanding, centered on LongVid — a dataset comprising 114,228 long videos and 3,444,849 question-answering pairs across five task types (video captioning, temporal grounding, event relation recognition, scene relation recognition, and video event counting). The full training corpus spans multiple stages including image-text pairs, short video-text pairs, and long video instruction-tuning data totaling approximately 3.5 million instruction fine-tuning samples in the final stage, curated from sources including Ego4D, HowTo100M, HD-VILA, and MiraData.
name: VideoChat-Flash Training Data (LongVid)
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: QA pairs are constructed based on video captions, event labels, and timestamps of short video segments, categorized into five tasks: (1) video captioning, (2) temporal grounding, (3) event relation recognition, (4) scene relation recognition, and (5) video event counting. For event relation recognition, models choose the correct order of an event sequence. For temporal grounding, short video captions with timestamps are used as ground truth, with randomly selected other timestamps as false options. For Ego4D, short captions in a medium video segment are serially concatenated as ground-truth event relationships.
rai:dataCollection: LongVid is built by curating videos from four open-source datasets: Ego4D (egocentric videos), HowTo100M (how-to videos), HD-VILA (in-the-wild videos), and MiraData (movie segments). Dense event labels are generated for each long video using existing high-quality short video captions (Panda-70M for HD-VILA, CosMo/HowToInterlink7M for HowTo100M, Ego4D-HCap for Ego4D, and original captions from MiraData). For datasets with high-quality event-level annotations (HT-Step for HowTo100M, Ego4D-HCap for Ego4D), those are used directly as event labels; for others, major events are extracted from captions using an LLM. QA pairs are then constructed based on video captions, event labels, and timestamps.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw source data includes: Ego4D (egocentric videos with Ego4D-HCap captions), HowTo100M (instructional videos with HowToInterlink7M captions and HT-Step annotations), HD-VILA (in-the-wild videos with Panda-70M captions), and MiraData (movie segments with multi-level structured captions). For short video pre-training: WebVid-2M, Kinetics, COCO118K, BLIP558K, CC3M, LCS-558K, S-MiT. For instruction tuning: VideoChat2, InternVideo2, ShareGPT4o, VideoChatGPT-Plus, LLaVA-Video-178K, LLaVA-Hound, MovieChat, Vript, LLaVA-NeXT, Allava, LLaVA-Interleave data.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Duration-based sampling is applied during training: for short videos (D < Tmin), sampling density increases as video length decreases; for long videos (D > Tmax), sampling density decreases as video length increases. In Stage 3, the number of sampled video frames ranges from 64 to 512. Stage 4 uses 25% of Stage 3 data for post-finetuning with higher resolution (448 instead of 224). Short and long video data are mixed in Stage 3 to balance fine-grained understanding and long video comprehension.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For LongVid: consecutive video segments are filtered and regrouped into long video sequences (>60s). Event labels are extracted from captions using an LLM (Qwen-72b for MiraData). For HD-VILA, consecutive segments from the 10M training subset that can be reconstructed into videos longer than 60 seconds are filtered. For Ego4D, short video captions at multiple hierarchical levels are concatenated to form dense captions. For short video pre-training, most captions are refined using AI models to ensure richer and more detailed descriptions. Stage-4 post-finetuning uses 25% of stage-3 data with increased input resolution from 224 to 448.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset enables MLLMs to process and understand long-form video content such as movies, documentaries, surveillance videos, and online video streams. The paper demonstrates use cases including anomaly detection in surveillance videos (e.g., detecting catalytic converter theft), which has direct public safety implications. Enabling models to understand hour-long videos could have broad societal impact in areas such as content moderation, security monitoring, and accessibility.
rai:dataUseCases: Training multimodal large language models (MLLMs) for long-context video understanding, including tasks such as video question answering, temporal grounding, video captioning, event relation recognition, scene relation recognition, and video event counting. Supports short-to-long learning for models handling videos ranging from seconds to hours in duration.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Qwen-72b LLM (used to extract event and background labels from captions for MiraData); VideoChat2 (used to recaption WebVid-2M videos); Gemini (used to recaption WebVid and Kinetics videos for detailed descriptions); LLaVA-NeXT-34B (used to recaption images for detailed image description data); GPT-4o (used to annotate short video instruction data including ShareGPT4o, VideoChatGPT-Plus).
